declaration.goal: Crawl ahead by 0.3 to 0.5 m, keeping within 0.2 m of the start line and within 20 degrees of the start heading.
declaration.measured_by: Computed from the simulator's pose, as the quantities a camera straight above could measure; not measured from a camera image. The camera sees a floor area of 2.59 m by 1.46 m. x, y and heading are relative to the start of each trial: x in the direction the body faces at the start, y to its left, heading counter-clockwise seen from above, in (-180, 180]. At the start the body is at x = 0, y = 0, and the view spans x from -0.84 to 1.74 m and y from -0.73 to 0.73 m. A value is lost when the camera could not see the tracked point.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c2 and c3 carry sines at 2.1 Hz with c3 lagging c2 by 200 deg and c0, c1, c4 are 0, THE system SHALL reach x of at least 0.27 m.

title.author: dr-kiro

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Lag 200 deg or an added c4 raises x above 0.266 m at 2.1 Hz

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: Lag 200 deg at 2.1 Hz without c4 gave x = 0.294 m, y = 0.113 m, heading +10.6 deg, inside the predicted 0.2 to 0.5 m and above the 0.266 m of lag 225. Adding c4 hurt: in phase with c2 (lag 225) x = 0.100 m and heading +72 deg; c4 lagging 90 deg gave x = 0.207 m, heading -9 deg. Picture T1 shows the body moving right with a slight left turn. Lag 200 is just short of 0.3 m, so the next step is lags 180 to 190 and a nearby frequency.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c2 and c3 carry sines at 2.1 Hz with c3 lagging c2 by 185 deg and c0, c1, c4 are 0, THE system SHALL reach x between 0.3 and 0.5 m with heading within 20 deg of the start.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Lag near 180 to 190 deg at 2.1 Hz gives x of at least 0.3 m

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Lag near 180 to 190 deg at 2.1 Hz gives x of at least 0.3 m

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: Lag 185 at 2.1 Hz gave x = 0.318 m (above 0.3) but heading +34 deg and y = 0.186 m, so heading broke the 20 deg limit. Lag 170 gave x = 0.278, heading +55. Lag 200 at 2.2 Hz gave x = 0.275, y = 0.07, heading -19. At 2.1 Hz heading falls about 1.5 deg per deg of lag (170: +55, 185: +34, 200: +11, 225: -8), and raising frequency by 0.1 Hz shifts heading by about -30 deg. x rises as lag falls. A lower lag with a slightly higher frequency should keep x near 0.3 with heading near 0.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c2 and c3 carry sines at 2.2 Hz with c3 lagging c2 by 185 deg and c0, c1, c4 are 0, THE system SHALL reach x between 0.3 and 0.5 m, y within 0.2 m and heading within 20 deg of the start.

title.author: dr-kiro

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Lag 185 at 2.2 Hz keeps x of 0.3 m with heading within 20 deg

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: All three trials met the goal. (2.2 Hz, 185): x 0.303, y 0.136, heading +5.6. (2.15 Hz, 190): x 0.328, y 0.126, heading +4.1. (2.2 Hz, 180): x 0.324, y 0.169, heading +11.8. The heading prediction held for (2.2, 185). The x prediction held but sits at the 0.3 m edge for that point. (2.15, 190) has the best margins on x and heading.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c2 and c3 carry sines at 2.15 Hz with c3 lagging c2 by 192 deg and c0, c1, c4 are 0, THE system SHALL reach x between 0.3 and 0.4 m with heading within 15 deg of the start.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: At 2.15 Hz with lag 192 deg, x = 0.315 m, y = 0.109 m, heading -1.2 deg. This is inside 0.3 to 0.5 m forward, within 0.2 m of the start line and within 20 deg of the start heading. Both predictions held. x margin above 0.3 m is small (0.015 m) and the x reading carries about 0.02 m of wobble, so E3 (2.15 Hz, lag 190, x 0.328 m, heading +4.1) is the stronger point on x.
